mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals fewer commuting trips and more time near home, which reduces discretionary retail visits over the next four weeks. The effect is strongest when RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, indicating persistent stay-at-home behavior rather than a temporary mode shift.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES staying below baseline and RESIDENTIAL staying above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-week drop in TRANSIT below the prior week's level by more than 5 points reduces spontaneous shopping access immediately, pushing RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks. This is a transport-access channel, not a broader demand shift.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days after a week-on-week TRANSIT drop greater than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES stays deeply depressed while GROCERY_PHARM remains closer to baseline, households substitute toward essential trips and away from leisure retail. That substitution keeps RETAIL_REC below its recent four-week average over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains at least 20 points below baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES stays at least 20 points below baseline for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained lift in PARKS mobility signals favorable weather and outdoor recreation, which crowds out enclosed retail visits and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The effect should appear when PARKS is rising faster than both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even as PARKS rises for two consecutive weeks and remains above its prior week.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility stays above baseline while RETAIL_REC keeps falling, then home-centered routines are crowding out shopping trips and the decline should continue for at least one more week. This is a short-lag persistence signal from staying home.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 12 points for one week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to remain below its current week level in the next 7 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above 12 points.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increases weekday foot traffic and generates a lagged rebound in retail visits over four weeks. The channel fails if only one of the two series improves, because retail demand depends on both commuting and worksite density.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES move upward from their current levels.

mechanism_narrative: A regime of sustained movement suppression, marked by TRANSIT below -40 and WORKPLACES below -25, implies mobility controls that directly depress discretionary shopping. Under that regime, RETAIL_REC should stay below the last four-week mean over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -40 and WORKPLACES below -25 for one week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-four-week average even though TRANSIT remains below -40 and WORKPLACES remains below -25 for a week.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM falls while RETAIL_REC also falls, consumers are shifting fewer overall errands into the city center, and retail softness should continue over the next two weeks. This is a demand-compression signal rather than a pure substitution into essentials.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM declines for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC turns upward within 14 days even though GROCERY_PHARM declines for two consecutive weeks.
